title: Polynomial bit-length machine
statement: For natural numbers $C$ and $e$, define a Boolean Turing machine as follows: if $C=0$, it emits the binary representation of $0$; if $C>0$ and $e=0$, it emits the binary representation of $C$; and if $C>0$ and $e>0$, it is the buffered composition of the unary polynomial generator with the machine that outputs the bit-length of its input.
caveat: The statement defines the machine by composition, but the supplied definitions do not specify the buffered-composition operation or the bit-length machine’s behavior in enough detail to give a more explicit operational description.
